knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates a binary aqueous electrolyte system of potassium acetate (KAc) and sodium acetate (NaAc) for sodium-ion batteries, specifically testing concentrations up to 20 mol kg⁻¹ KAc and 7 mol kg⁻¹ NaAc. Carbon-coated LiTi2(PO4)3 (CLTP) is synthesized via a one-pot method and used as an electrode material to study alkaline ion intercalation. The electrolytes are prepared by dissolving high-purity salts in Milli-Q water, with specific compositions labeled 1N20K, 2.5N20K, 5N20K, and 7N20K.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes the thermal and transport properties of highly concentrated aqueous acetate electrolytes, noting that increased salt concentration shifts the glass transition temperature (Tg) to higher values, transitioning the system from salt-in-water to water-in-salt characteristics. The most concentrated sample, 7N20K, exhibits a conductivity of 21.2 mS cm⁻¹ at 25°C and prevents premature cell failure by avoiding salt crystallization during long-term cycling. Ionic conductivity follows Vogel-Tamman-Fulcher behavior, with the ideal glass transition temperature (T₀) correlating with the DSC-measured Tg and increasing with concentration due to higher activation barriers for ion movement.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study classifies the tested aqueous acetate electrolytes as quasi-ideal, with the most concentrated sample (7N20K) adhering to Kohlrausch's law at 25°C. Electrochemical stability windows were determined via linear sweep voltammetry, showing increased cathodic stability with higher salt concentration due to suppressed hydrogen evolution. A carbon-coated NASICON electrode was synthesized and characterized to demonstrate the feasibility of using the 7N20K electrolyte in sodium-ion batteries.
